claim:
GENERATION A/B (Tier 1, D341): does weighting the regime draw by BOOK-USABLE rate beat weighting it by COMPONENT rate? Two maps, one grammar, both drawing inside EVERY batch, each config tagged `generation_arm` ("baseline" = the incumbent component-rate map learned from Crucible's gated-runs export; "book_usable" = regime gates scored by P(cpcv >= 0.9439) on our honest arm).

REGISTERED LATE, AND THE INTERIM IS DISCLOSED — read this before the numbers. This A/B was built, deployed and left accruing WITHOUT a pre-registration, unlike the tail and trend lanes which both had one. That was an omission, not a design choice. At the moment of registration an interim read had ALREADY been taken at n=1,123/arm: p90 0.6348 (book_usable) vs 0.5625 (baseline), delta +0.0723, bootstrap P(delta<=0) = 0.001; book-usable rate 11/1,123 = 0.98% vs 9/1,122 = 0.80%, z = +0.45; medians 0.1445 vs 0.1376. Registering after a favourable peek is strictly weaker than registering before one, and no reading of this prereg should pretend otherwise. It is recorded here so the weakness is visible in the artifact rather than discoverable only from commit timestamps.

WHY CONCURRENT ARMS AT ALL. A weighting change evaluated across TIME confounds the change with the measurement window: Crucible's drift floor puts version-over-version deltas below ~0.15-0.20 beyond resolution at ANY n, because the noise is BETWEEN windows and does not shrink with sample size. Our own honest medians read v49 0.1656, v50 0.1543, v51 0.2167 across different weeks and cannot be attributed. The two-leg ranked lane is the proof the fix works — same batches, same days, only the objective differing, read at z=+6.27 where a before/after read would have been unusable.

WHY THE QUESTION IS OPEN RATHER THAN OBVIOUS. The incumbent map scores a regime gate by COMPONENT rate on RANKER-SELECTED runs — a collider-conditioned population (D337/D338). Arm B scores by BOOK-USABLE rate on the honest arm, the only population unselected by both prefilter and ranker. On live data the two maps disagree by ~9x across gates (vol_regime 2.87 down to vix_term_slope 0.31). But a dispersion test says per-CELL rates are NOT distinguishable from a single common rate (X2=38.9, df=37, z=+0.29), so arm B's estimator shrinks a cell to its REGIME MARGINAL below n=100 — the regime marginal being the level where signal does exist (z=+2.16).

PRIMARY METRIC: p90 of cpcv on the honest arm (`selection_mode='prefilter_sample'`), STAGE ONE only, never pooled with the refit lane. p90 is chosen because it resolves — a +0.05 move needs ~2,425/arm (~3 days at the pre-ramp rate) — whereas the 1.5-gate exceedance rate needs 183 days/arm and cannot be a decision metric at our throughput. The book-usable EXCEEDANCE RATE is reported as a secondary, explicitly underpowered at these counts (the interim z=+0.45 on 11-vs-9 events).

PREDICTION: at the resolution point, arm B's honest-arm p90 exceeds arm A's, with a bootstrap P(delta <= 0) < 0.05 over 2,000 resamples.

RESOLUTION RULE, FIXED IN ADVANCE OF FURTHER DATA: a SINGLE read once BOTH arms reach n = 2,000 decided honest stage-one configs. No peeking-to-threshold, no early call if the number looks good, no extension if it does not. The n is set from the power calculation for a +0.05 effect, deliberately NOT from the +0.0723 observed in the interim — sizing an experiment on the effect you have already seen in it is circular.

FALSIFIER: if arm B's p90 does not exceed arm A's at that n, or the bootstrap does not clear 0.05, the book-usable weighting does not beat the incumbent component-rate map and the arm is reverted to a single map. A null is a real outcome here and the incumbent keeps the draw.

THE CAVEAT THIS TEST CANNOT SETTLE, stated so it is not discovered later: arm B's weights are FITTED ON THE SAME HONEST ARM the read is taken from. Some of any p90 edge may be in-sample co-movement rather than prediction. The concurrent split removes the drift confound but NOT this one; only a forward window on weights frozen before the read would. If arm B wins, that is the next experiment, not a promotion of the weighting to permanent default.

SECOND CAVEAT: the primary and secondary metrics currently DISAGREE (p90 bootstrap 0.001 vs floor-rate z=+0.45), and the floor rate is the metric arm B was actually built to move. If that disagreement persists at the resolution n, the honest reading is that arm B shifts the upper-middle of the distribution without producing more book-usable components — which is a weaker claim than "the weighting works" and must not be reported as the stronger one.
